chapter: Ellington colleagues, singers and world tours
title: His Fleetwood Cabriolet
summary: He bought a sixteen-cylinder Cadillac in 1931, stored it for twenty years and logged only 32,000 miles.

story.theme_name: Life on the road: touring bands, buses and one-nighters
story.community_name: Life on the road: buses, trains and one-nighters

blocks.x: Barney Bigard was talking about you, and he said that, when you joined the band -- I guess it was right about the time you joined the band -- that you were so proud of a very big, beautiful, shiny Cadillac you had.

Yes, I used to be car crazy and just went from one car to another, and I guess he's talking about a 16 cylinder, Fleetwood Cabriolet that I bought in '31, and, of course, after I left in '32 I had to put it in dead storage in different garages, like the Richfield Garage downtown, different places like that. I kept it in places where all I had to do was to telephone in or wire in and tell them to get it ready. Then when I got here, it would be ready to hit the street.
How long did you keep the car?
Hah. About 20 years and had a terrific 32,000 miles at the end of it.
You spent so little time in Los
Yeah, just a few days at a time.
